name: Firecracker Jailer
description: Privileged setup binary that wraps Firecracker. Sets up cgroups, chroot, network namespace, and resource limits, drops privileges to a low uid/gid, then exec()s into the Firecracker binary. Production-deployment-mandatory wrapper — design.md states 'Firecracker should only run constrained at the process level' achieved via the jailer.

name: Statically linked Firecracker pairing
description: Each jailer binary must be paired with a STATICALLY linked Firecracker (default musl toolchain) of the SAME version. Mixing dynamically-linked Firecracker (experimental gnu builds) is unsupported — symbol resolution inside the chroot may fail because libraries aren't copied in.

name: Chroot jail layout
description: Jailer creates `<chroot_base>/<exec_file_name>/<id>/root` (default chroot_base=/srv/jailer). Copies the Firecracker binary into the chroot (so each microVM has its own non-shared mapping). Switches mount namespace via unshare() + pivot_root() + chroot(). The microVM's API socket, log/metrics FIFOs, and snapshot files all live INSIDE this chroot.

name: Privilege drop (uid/gid)
description: Jailer setuid/setgid to a non-privileged uid/gid before exec()ing Firecracker. Once dropped, Firecracker can only access resources granted to that uid (e.g., chroot tree, /dev/kvm if kvm-group has access). Critical defense-in-depth: KVM compromise is constrained to the jailed uid's reach.

name: Cgroup setup (v1 + v2)
description: Jailer creates a cgroup `<cgroup_base>/<parent_cgroup>/<id>` and writes the Firecracker pid to its tasks file. Supports both cgroup-v1 (--cgroup-version=1, default) and v2. Caller specifies cgroup values via repeated --cgroup flag (e.g. cpuset.cpus=0,cpu.shares=512). Lets orchestrators bound CPU/memory/IO without separate root operations.

name: cgroup-v2 subtree-control trap
description: If using --cgroup-version=2 with --parent-cgroup pointing at an existing cgroup, the jailer attempts to MOVE the process there. If that cgroup has domain controllers (e.g., memory) enabled in cgroup.subtree_control, the move fails with 'no internal process constraint' — exit error. Workaround: leave subtree_control empty or move to a leaf cgroup.

name: Network namespace join (--netns)
description: When --netns <path> is given, jailer setns()s into the network namespace at that path before exec()ing Firecracker. Combined with TAP devices created INSIDE that netns, this gives each microVM its own network stack — no leakage between sandboxes.

name: Resource limits (setrlimit)
description: --resource-limit fsize=<N> or no-file=<N> applies setrlimit() on the Firecracker process before exec. fsize bounds max file size (use to prevent runaway snapshot files); no-file bounds max FD count. Default no-file is 2048 if unspecified — sufficient for moderate microVM device counts but may need raising for vsock-heavy or VirtIO-MMIO-heavy guests.

name: --daemonize flag
description: Jailer calls setsid() and redirects stdin/stdout/stderr to /dev/null. Detaches from controlling terminal. Useful when launching Firecracker from a non-systemd orchestrator that doesn't handle daemonization itself.

name: --new-pid-ns flag (PID namespace)
description: Spawns Firecracker into a fresh PID namespace via clone(CLONE_NEWPID). Inside the jail, the Firecracker process appears as PID 1 with no visibility into other host processes. The host-side PID is recorded in `<chroot_dir>/<exec_file_name>.pid` for the orchestrator to track.

name: FD + env cleanup before exec
description: Jailer closes ALL open fds except 0/1/2 (per /proc/<jailer-pid>/fd) and clears all environment variables before pivoting to the chroot and exec()ing Firecracker. Prevents leaking parent-process state — orchestrator-side fds, secrets in env vars, etc. — into the sandbox.

name: /dev passthrough via mknod
description: Inside the chroot, jailer mknod()s `/dev/net/tun` and `/dev/kvm` so Firecracker can open them. These are the ONLY two devices the jail exposes — minimum surface for VirtIO-net (TAP) and KVM (the hypervisor itself). No other /dev entries.
